title: How Much Fiber in Sweet Potato? 3.8g per Medium
description: Sweet Potato: about 3.8 g of fiber per 1 medium, baked (13% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in sweet potato?

answer.note: USDA FoodData Central, Sweet potato, cooked, baked in skin, flesh, without salt

intro: Sweet potato ranks #9 of 10 vegetables on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in sweet potato by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in sweet potato?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists sweet potato, cooked, baked in skin, flesh, without salt at 3.3 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (1 medium, baked (flesh); 114 g) therefore has about 3.8 g of fiber and 103 calories. That is 13% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 15% of a 25 g day and 10% of a 38 g day.
A baked sweet potato gives a few grams of fiber along with plenty of vitamin A. Larger sweet potatoes, which are common in U.S. stores, can easily be twice the USDA medium.

sections.heading: Skin on and portion size
paragraphs: USDA’s baked sweet potato entry is for the flesh only. The skin is edible and adds some fiber, so eating it gives a bit more than the table shows.

Sweet potato fries and casseroles change the picture: frying adds fat, and casseroles add sugar and butter. The fiber per cup of sweet potato is similar, but the portion of actual potato is often smaller.

sections.heading: How sweet potato compares with other vegetables
paragraphs: Of the 10 vegetables on this site, sweet potato ranks #9 for fiber per typical serving and #9 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 3.7 g of fiber per 100 calories, a high ratio: you get a lot of fiber for the calories.

Close neighbors by serving: [baked potato](/fiber-in-potato) at 3.8 g (1 medium, baked, flesh and skin); [green beans](/fiber-in-green-beans) at 4 g (1 cup, cooked); [Brussels sprouts](/fiber-in-brussels-sprouts) at 4.1 g (1 cup, cooked). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), sweet potato is #33 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding sweet potato to your day
paragraphs: Top a baked sweet potato with black beans and serve with cooked greens for a meal in the 15 g range.

Example: 1 sweet potato, 1/2 cup black beans, 1 cup cooked spinach. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 15.6 g of fiber, with 3.8 g from the sweet potato. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of sweet potato?
faqs.a: 3.3 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Sweet potato, cooked, baked in skin, flesh, without salt). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in sweet potato (1 cup, baked (flesh))?
faqs.a: About 6.6 g, for 200 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.

faqs.q: Sweet potato vs white potato for fiber?
faqs.a: Similar per medium potato. A baked white potato with skin is about 3.8 g (1 medium, baked, flesh and skin); a medium baked sweet potato is about 3.8 g (1 medium, baked (flesh)).

faqs.q: Should I eat sweet potato skin?
faqs.a: If you enjoy it, yes. Wash it well before baking. The skin adds fiber.
